THESE APPEALS ARE COMING ON FOR ADMISSION,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT M.F.A.No.102114/2017 is the appeal preferred by the insurance company and M.F.A.No.103593/2017 is the appeal preferred by claimant.

Aggrieved by the very same judgment in M.V.C.No.737/2015 dated 20.01.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Ballari (for short 'the Tribunal'), the appeal preferred by the insurer is on the ground of excessive compensation awarded to the claimant as being exorbitant.
Appeal preferred by the claimant is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 18.06.2015, at about 06.00 p.m. when the claimant was proceeding along with one Govinda on his TVS Star City Motorcycle, as a pillion rider from Sirigedoddi village towards Rayadurga, at that time, when they reached at Sirigedoddi village,
Gummagatta Mandalam, respondent No.1, who was driving the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg. No.KA-16/B-7058 came from Rayadurga side in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and safety, dashed against the motorcycle, in which the claimant was a pillion rider.

Due to the impact of the accident, the claimant as well as rider of the motorcycle fell down and sustained Grade-I compound fracture of right tibia lower 1/3rd with compound fracture of 1st metatarsal with crush injury over foot.
Immediately thereafter, claimant shifted to Community Health Centre, Rayadurga, where he was admitted.
Thereafter, he was admitted to Sanjeevini Hospital, Ballari, where the claimant took treatment as an inpatient from 19.06.2015 to 22.06.2015.
It is stated that during the course of treatment, major operation was conducted on the right leg and steel rods and plates were inserted.
Pursuant to which, claimant took continuous follow up treatment with the private doctors for a long time.
4. It is stated that claimant incurred a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical and other miscellaneous expenses.

It is the case of claimant that he was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and he was doing coolie work, earning a sum of Rs.400/- per day and was contributing his earnings for the welfare of maintenance of his family.
It is also stated that he is only earning member of his family and due to the accident and the injuries suffered by him, he is not in a position to either walk or work as before.
It is also stated that due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident, he has lost his earning capacity as he was prior to the date of occurrence of accident.
Due to the occurrence of accident and the injuries suffered, the claimant preferred claim petition claiming compensation against the respondents.

sentences.text: On notice being issued, respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their detailed statement of objections inter alia denying the contentions putforth by the claimant.

It is the statement of respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle that since his vehicle is insured with respondent No.3 and if any liability is fastened on him, the same will have to be indemnified by respondent No.3- insurer.
Respondent No.3 however filed separate statement of objections inter alia denying all the contentions made by the claimant.
However, it admitted the insurance policy being in force with regard to respondent No.2.

However, he denied the occurrence of accident, the age,
avocation of claimant and the medical expenses having incurred by the claimant and that the claim petition was bad for mis-joinder and non joinder of proper and necessary parties.
So also contended that the claim made by the claimant was excessive and exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal has framed relevant issues for consideration.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and also examined the doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

However,
the respondents have not led any evidence neither have produced any material on their behalf.

8. On the basis of the material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.7,20,680/- to be jointly and severally paid by the respondent Nos.1 to 3 with interest @ 7% p.a. to the claimant.
However, directed the 3rd respondent being the insurer to deposit the compensation amount in view of the insurance police being in force.

9. Being aggrieved by the exorbitant amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the erroneous calculations of disability by PW.2 and the Tribunal calculating the disability at 40%, the insurance company is in appeal challenging the same.

Whereas, claimant has approached this Court,
seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground of meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

10. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel appearing for the insurer that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering the material evidence on record both oral and documentary and has erred in calculating the disability to an extent of 40% without there being any reasonable basis or clinical assessment to that effect.

It is further contended by the learned counsel for the Insurer that the Tribunal has committed an error in not taking into consideration the evidence of Doctor P.W.2 and has awarded disability to an extent of 40% which is highly erroneous and without any medical and clinical analysis put forth by the Doctor.
It is further contended by the learned counsel that the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation on all other heads.
Therefore, the question of enhancement of compensation under other heads does not arise.
He further contends that the Tribunal has awarded suitable compensation based on the material evidence placed by the claimant.
Therefore, enhancement sought for by the claimant in the connected appeal does not deserve to be considered as just and reasonable compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the Insurer seeks to allow his appeal and dismiss the appeal preferred by the claimant.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- claimant vehemently contends that the Tribunal has committed a gross error in not appreciating the material evidence both oral and documentary and has awarded meager compensation including the assessment of income of the claimant, which is on the lower side.

Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal ought to have taken income at Rs.12,000/- per month as he was a coolie and since the claimant has undergone surgery due to serious injuries with crush injury to the right foot and fracture of his right leg.

He is unable to stand,
walk and climb steps up and down and perform daily routine agriculture works.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded just and reasonable compensation, whereas the Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.6,000/- per month which is on the lower side.

12. Learned counsel for the claimant further contends that the assessment made by the Doctor,
P.W.2, is correct in view of the fact that the claimant has sustained Grade I compound fracture of right tibia lower 1/3rd with compound fracture of 1st metatarsal bone with crush injury to foot.

It is vehement contention of the claimant that since the claimant has sustained grievous crush injury on his right foot and question of him getting back to his work and perform his normal day today activities in the agriculture field as a coolie is totally ruled out in view of the serious injuries.
Therefore, it is his contention that the Doctor P.W.2 has rightly assessed the disability to n extent of 45%.
The same requires to be awarded whereas the Tribunal has reduced the percentage of disability to extent of 40% which is erroneous in law.

13. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has not awarded suitable compensation under the head of loss of income during treatment period so also no amount of compensation is awarded under the head of nourishment, attendant charges and extra nourishment - 10 - during period of treatment.

It is also contended by learned counsel that the Tribunal has erred in not awarding future medical expenses as claimed by him in view of the fact that he is required to further undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding suitable compensation under the head loss of amenities.
On these grounds, he seeks to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation and dismissing the appeal filed by the Insurer.

14. Having heard the learned counsel for the claimant and learned counsel for Insurer, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
"i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation?
ii) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?

iii) What order?"
15.
It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 18.06.2015 whiling claimant was riding the motorcycle.

When the respondent No.1 being the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck came from the M/S. Shriram General Insurance Company ... vs Palaiah @ K Pala Nayaka on 30 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90987655/

sentences.text: To substantiate this aspect of the matter, the claimant has examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 5.
These are all Police records which are pursuant to the enquiry and investigation conducted by the jurisdictional police.
In the present case on hand, there is no serious dispute with regard to liability, occurrence of accident and the rash and negligence by the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck.

Hence, this Court would not delve into the occurrence of accident,
the rash and negligence and the liability fastened on the Insurance Company.
16. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the claimant, it is not in dispute that the claimant was a coolie.
Though, it is claimed that the claimant was earning Rs.400/- per day.
He has not produced any material evidence before the Tribunal or this Court to prove the same.

Hence,
under the circumstances, the Tribunal has taken notional income of Rs.6,000/- per month to assess the compensation.

In a case where there is no proof of income, the Tribunal as well as this Court are left with no other option but to do guess work and same will have to be done in the standard manner for which the Legal Services Authority has prescribed the notional income for the - 12 - relevant year of accident.

In the present case the accident having occurred in the year 2015,
Rs.8,000/- per month would be the income adopted for the relevant year.
In view of the same, I deem it appropriate to assess the income of the claimant at Rs.8,000/- per month as against Rs.6,000/- per month assessed by the Tribunal.
17. The claimant has got examined Doctor as P.W.2, who has stated on oath that he has issued disability certificate mentioning the disability to the extent of 45% as per Ex.P.6.

It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained fracture of Grade I compound fracture of right tibia lower 1/3rd with compound fracture of 1st metatarsal bone with crush injury of right foot and that he is unable to do his work as he was able to do prior to the date of occurrence of accident.
It is also not in dispute that P.W.2, Doctor is not the Doctor who treated the claimant.

However, the evidence of Doctor depicts that he is an Orthopedic Surgeon, who on the basis of examination has arrived at conclusion that the claimant has difficulty in walking, climbing up and down stairs, difficult in squatting and sitting crossed legs, difficulty in cycling, restricted movement of knee joint and ankle joint and foot - 13 - movement.
He has also assessed there is non union of tibia and fibula with implant in situ with mal-union of right foot 1st MIB.
On the basis of these analysis and examination he has arrived at partial permanent disability to an extent of 45% to the whole body of the claimant.

18. On analysis of evidence of P.W.2, the Tribunal has assessed the disability to be at 40%
considering the fact that the Doctor, P.W.2 is not the person who treated the claimant.

However,

sentences.text: there is no finding with regard to why the disability assessed by the Doctor has been reduced from 45% to 40% to the whole body in the findings of the Tribunal.

Learned counsel appearing for the insurer vehemently contends that when an analysis is made by the Doctor who deposes before the Court, he has to make it on the basis of his personal interaction when the operation or having treated/the claimant he himself or by comparing the x-ray and treatment given to the claimant.
In the present case on hand, the Doctor P.W.2 is not the Doctor who treated the claimant and hence he contends that the assessment of disability to an extent of 45% is on the higher side.
No doubt, P.W.2 is not the Doctor who treated the claimant, but however he has deposed before the Court - 14 - as an expert in Orthopedics and he is an Orthopedic Surgeon.
On the basis of analysis and report he has stated the medical condition of the claimant.
On the basis of Wound Certificate and the examination analysis is forthcoming in the evidence deposed by him.

The question that requires to be considered by this Court is whether the assessment of disability at 45% made by the Doctor P.W.2 is exorbitant and whether the same requires to be reduced further than what is awarded by the Tribunal to the extent of 40%.
19.

On a careful analysis of the entire medical records of the claimant and the assessment of evidence made by the Doctor P.W.2, it is borne that the claimant has suffered severe fracture of tibia bone of lower 1/3rd of the right leg and compound fracture of 1st metatarsal bone and crush injury of right foot.
Due to which, the claimant is unable to walk on right foot.
He will have to use crutches on one side for his day to day works.

In view of the crush injury on the right foot, the Tribunal has considered the aspect of evidence adduced by the Doctor with regard to the magnitude of injury suffered by the claimant and assessed the disability to the extent of 40%.

There is some force in - 15 - the contention put forth by the learned counsel for the insurer that the Doctor who deposed before the Court as P.W.2 has admittedly not taken into consideration the X- rays, medical records and neither he is the Doctor who treated the patient.
Therefore, the disability assessed by the Doctor appears to be on the higher side and same requires to be reduced to marginal extent considering magnitude of injuries sustained by the claimant.
I am of the view that disability could be assessed at 25% rather than 40% awarded by the Tribunal.

20. It is not in dispute that the claimant is aged 23 years as on the date of accident and the appropriate multiplier applicable in the case on hand would be '18' as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, which has been rightly adopted by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Towards loss of income during laid up period, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.6,000/-, which is on the lower side and I am in agreement with the contentions put forth by the learned counsel for claimant, same requires to be increased.

In view of this Court having increased the income of the claimant to Rs.8,000/- per month considering the fact that the claimant would required at least 3 months period to recuperate to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Hence, (Rs.8,000/- X 3 months) a sum of Rs.24,000/- is awarded under this head as against Rs.6,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
23. Towards food, nourishment and conveyance charges, the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- under this head.
24. Towards future medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.
There is no evidence by the Doctor as to the future medical expenses to be meted out.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
25. Towards loss of unhappiness and amenities, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- which is on the lower - 17 - side same is enhanced to Rs.22,000/- as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

26. Towards future prospects, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- it is seriously contended by the learned counsel for the insurer that this amount is highly erroneous in view of the fact that already the Tribunal has awarded loss of future earning capacity due to the permanent disability.
Hence, this amount requires to be set at naught.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for insurer that this is to be set at naught, accordingly it is set at naught.
27. Towards pain and agony, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/-.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the said amount, same is left intact.
28. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for Insurer that the interest awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side same requires to be reduced to 6% per annum.

Therefore, the disability assessed by the Doctor appears to be on the higher side and same requires to be reduced to marginal extent considering magnitude of injuries sustained by the claimant.
I am of the view that disability could be assessed at 25% rather than 40% awarded by the Tribunal.

7 Rs.8,000/- X 12 X 18 X 25/100 = Rs.4,32,000/-.
- 16 - 22.
Hence, (Rs.8,000/- X 3 months) a sum of Rs.24,000/- is awarded under this head as against Rs.6,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
23. Towards food, nourishment and conveyance charges, the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- under this head.
24. Towards future medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
25. Towards loss of unhappiness and amenities, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- which is on the lower - 17 - side same is enhanced to Rs.22,000/- as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, this amount requires to be set at naught.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for insurer that this is to be set at naught, accordingly it is set at naught.
27. Towards pain and agony, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/-.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the said amount, same is left intact.
28. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for Insurer that the interest awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side same requires to be reduced to 6% per annum.
29. In view of the above discussions, the claimant would be entitled for enhancement of compensation as mentioned in the table below:

naught Towards future medical 10,000 20,000 expenses

Towards loss of future 5,18,400 4,32,000 earning capacity on account of permanent disability Towards unhappiness and 10,000/- 22,000 loss of amenities Towards food, nourishment - 15,000 and conveyance charges.

ORDER i) Both the appeals are disposed off by modifying the Judgment and Award passed on 20.01.2017 in M.V.C.No.737/2015 by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Ballari.
ii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,89,280/- as against Rs.7,20,680/- awarded by the Tribunal;
- 19 - iii) The interest awarded on the compensation amount by the Tribunal is reduced from 7% per annum to 6% per annum;
iv) The entire amount deposited before this Court shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional M.A.C.T.
v) The award amount as modified by this Court shall be disbursed to the claimant in accordance to the terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal.
The balance amount, if any shall be refunded to the Insurer.
vi) Registry to transmit the records to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
